Companion animal travel desk guidance

Aurelia Skyways reviews companion travel with safety in mind, and we want each trip to feel steady and predictable. The most helpful preparation is to keep your pet's needs simple, consistent, and easy for staff to verify. A calm plan also reduces stress during check-in and boarding.

Please gather your travel documents, feeding notes, and any comfort items that are allowed for the journey. Keep the carrier clean, secure, and sized for safe movement. If your pet has a special routine, write it in clear language so the team can follow it without guesswork.

Pack only what is needed for the trip, and avoid loose items that may shift or spill. Water, absorbent liners, and familiar bedding can help support comfort. If your companion is sensitive to noise, movement, or unfamiliar handling, let the desk know early so care can be matched to temperament and species.

At check-in, the team will review the details and confirm the next steps. <<FACT F092>> Arrive with enough space in your planning to allow for any review that may be needed. If a document is missing or a carrier does not meet safety standards, the process may pause until the concern is resolved.

For the best outcome, keep your pet settled before travel and avoid sudden changes to feeding or routine unless your veterinarian has advised otherwise. A brief walk or quiet rest before departure can also help some animals remain comfortable. Staff members will look for signs of distress and may ask you to confirm handling notes before boarding.

If you are traveling with more than one companion, keep each plan separate and clearly labeled. This makes it easier for the welcome team to match each animal with the right support and reduces the risk of confusion during handoff.

If you need more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk for guidance before you travel.
